note: The four questions, declared as criteria rather than inferred from the files. Each names the input it requires. A question whose input is absent is refused, not estimated — a guessed verdict on a file store is worse than no verdict, because it gets acted on.

questions.asks: Is this file the same content as another file?
questions.rule: Two records are duplicates when their content hashes are equal. Same name is not duplication. Same size is not duplication.

questions.asks: Is this file a version of another file?
questions.rule: Two records are iterations of one work when their normalised stems are equal and their content hashes differ. Order is by modification time. The newest is the head; the rest are its history.

degraded.when: stem_rules not confirmed by the owner
degraded.reason: Normalisation is the whole question. A default ruleset that strips ' copy', ' (1)', ' final', ' v2' is a guess about one person's naming cadence, and the owner has stated that cadence is unreliable. Guessing it and then reporting confidently is how a file store gets reorganised into a worse one.

questions.asks: Does this file exist only once, as itself?
questions.rule: A record is novel when its content hash appears exactly once in the manifest and its normalised stem appears exactly once.

degraded.reason: Unique content is a fact about bytes. Novel is a claim about the work, and a work can be novel in content while being the fourth attempt at the same thing.

questions.asks: Is this file currently doing something?
questions.rule: A record is functional when something outside it refers to it: a page links it, a document cites it, a project embeds it, a release ships it, a post used it.

degraded.reason: This is the one question the filesystem cannot answer. Bytes, names and timestamps are all internal to the file. Function is a relation to something else. The owner's own diagnosis names it exactly — the files are 'not referenced or standardized' — and the missing reference is not a gap in the report, it is the finding.

load_bearing: Three of the four questions are answerable from a manifest of bytes. The fourth is not answerable from any manifest, at any resolution, ever. Building an index of what refers to what is a separate and larger job than scanning a drive, and no amount of scanning substitutes for it.
